findings: PinnedVersions derives `prop_name` directly from a JSON-pointer path segment and passes it to `remove_prop` without decoding JSON Pointer escapes. Keys containing `/` or `~` (notably scoped package names such as `@scope/pkg`, represented as `@scope~1pkg` in a pointer) will be removed using the escaped literal rather than the actual object key, so the pinned override remains.
evidence: The new code sets `prop_name = &path_to_prop[parent_path + 1..]`; no `~1`/`~0` decoding occurs before `package.remove_prop(parent_pointer, prop_name)`.
The prior VersionsByName path passes `self.descriptor.name`, which is the logical dependency/property name rather than a pointer token.
checked: PinnedVersions removal path splitting and property-key handling
gaps: No test evidence is supplied for removal of pinned entries whose key is scoped or otherwise requires JSON Pointer escaping.
